current.market_category: Commercial lease occupancy / NPV comparison for tenant-representation brokers
current.customer_segment: US tenant-representation and boutique CRE brokers
current.primary_job_to_be_done: Compare lease occupancy scenarios and communicate deal NPV without a one-off spreadsheet

competitors.name: ARGUS Enterprise / ARGUS Intelligence (Altus Group)
competitors.customer_segment: Institutional CRE investors, owners, lenders, and valuation teams
competitors.primary_offer: Property valuation, cash-flow forecasting, and portfolio performance management

observed_pricing.display: UNKNOWN — official price is contact-sales; no public rate card
observed_pricing.note: Altus states ARGUS Enterprise is no longer sold standalone and does not publish a public price.

competitors.free_tier_or_trial: UNKNOWN — not published as a self-serve free tier
competitors.positioning: Industry-standard institutional CRE valuation platform, not a tenant-rep deal NPV tool
weaknesses: enterprise implementation burden for boutique tenant-rep desks
competitors.differentiation_opportunity: OccupancyNPV targets per-deal tenant-rep NPV comparison at published $290/$149 prices versus institutional software.

competitors.name: Prophia
competitors.customer_segment: Owners, REITs, and institutional portfolio teams
competitors.primary_offer: Lease abstraction and portfolio lease-data platform

observed_pricing.display: UNKNOWN — official page is custom/contact-us; no public dollar amount
observed_pricing.note: Prophia pricing page lists Essentials as per-tenant annual subscription without a published dollar price.

competitors.positioning: Owner-side lease data and portfolio analytics, not tenant-rep NPV comparison
competitors.differentiation_opportunity: OccupancyNPV models tenant occupancy economics for a single deal rather than abstracting owner portfolios.

competitors.name: Occupier
competitors.customer_segment: Corporate tenants and occupier real-estate teams
competitors.primary_offer: Tenant lease administration, deal tracking, and ASC 842 accounting

observed_pricing.display: UNKNOWN — quote-based; no official public rate card found
observed_pricing.note: Vendor does not publish a self-serve price. Secondary writeups describe per-lease modules; those amounts are not treated as official.

competitors.positioning: Corporate occupier operating system, not a broker occupancy-NPV calculator
competitors.differentiation_opportunity: OccupancyNPV is a priced, self-serve occupancy NPV comparison for brokers, not lease accounting.

substitutes.name: Microsoft Excel / Google Sheets manual lease models

observed_pricing.display: UNKNOWN — spreadsheet software is general-purpose; lease-model cost is labor, not a product SKU
observed_pricing.note: Status-quo workflow confirmed as the incumbent process. No lease-NPV product price exists to observe.

substitutes.positioning: Default broker workflow OccupancyNPV is built to replace
substitutes.differentiation_opportunity: Productized occupancy NPV with published Professional and Per-Deal offers.
substitutes.evidence_source: OccupancyNPV primary offer: lease-scenario NPV comparison for tenant-representation brokers

substitutes.name: Lextract
substitutes.customer_segment: Brokers and analysts needing structured lease data

observed_pricing.note: Vendor comparison page publishes $15 per lease with no subscription. Abstraction is not occupancy NPV.

substitutes.free_tier_or_trial: Self-serve, no contract claimed on vendor page
substitutes.positioning: Data extraction substitute, not economic comparison
weaknesses: does not compute occupancy NPV or deal economics
substitutes.differentiation_opportunity: OccupancyNPV prices the decision model, not the PDF extraction.

monetization_models.rationale: Per-Deal is a live $149 one-time offer.
Lextract-style per-lease abstraction is adjacent, not OccupancyNPV's live model.
ARGUS/Prophia enterprise motion is the expensive incumbent, not OccupancyNPV's published path.

current.recommended_monetization_model: Dual offer: annual Professional subscription + one-time Per-Deal
current.recommended_pricing_hypothesis: Keep live $290/year and $149 one-time. Do not change prices. Competitive institutional tools are contact-sales / far higher secondary estimates; that does not prove WTP or CAC.

current.market_category: Local-business review request kits / reputation-adjacent utility
current.customer_segment: Owners of local shops, salons, restaurants, and service offices
current.primary_job_to_be_done: Generate reusable Google review links, QR, and request copy without buying an enterprise reputation suite

competitors.name: Birdeye
competitors.customer_segment: Multi-location and local businesses buying reputation suites
competitors.primary_offer: Review monitoring, listings, and reputation automation

observed_pricing.display: UNKNOWN official rate card; secondary reports ~$299/month starting points
observed_pricing.note: Birdeye does not publish a complete official rate card. Secondary 2026 writeups cite advertised starting points near $299/month. That is category context, not AskReview WTP.

competitors.differentiation_opportunity: AskReview hypothesizes a cheaper kit utility; $29/month remains HYPOTHESIS.

competitors.name: Podium
competitors.customer_segment: Local service businesses buying messaging + reviews
competitors.primary_offer: SMS-first inbox, payments, and review requests

observed_pricing.display: UNKNOWN official rate card; secondary reports ~$399/month starting points
observed_pricing.note: Podium pricing is quote-based. Secondary 2026 writeups cite advertised starting points near $399/month. Not AskReview willingness-to-pay.

competitors.differentiation_opportunity: AskReview does not send SMS/email; hypothesized kit-only price is unproven.

substitutes.name: Manual Google review requests (status quo)
substitutes.customer_segment: Local shops already asking for Google reviews by hand
substitutes.primary_offer: Owner texts or prints a Google review link

observed_pricing.note: Google Business Profile review links are free. Labor/time cost of asking is unmeasured and not treated as zero operating cost for AskReview.

substitutes.differentiation_opportunity: Reusable authenticated kits — only if operators will pay, which is unproven.

monetization_models.rationale: $29/month is a hypothesis to test, not a canonical price.
$49 one-time location kit is an untested alternative.
No experiment has compared free vs paid kits.

current.recommended_pricing_hypothesis: $29/month HYPOTHESIS; $49 one-time HYPOTHESIS. Do not resolve. Do not create Stripe prices.
